81: - **Assessment:** Grade 5 for provider-documented behavior; reviewed 2026-10-18; novelty moderate (directory already links OHLC, this adds precise cap and stream distinction). Source type: commercial exchange API documentation.
82: 
83: ### Coinbase Exchange public market data
84: 
85: - **Direct verified URLs:** [product candles](https://docs.cdp.coinbase.com/exchange/rest-api/market-data/get-product-candles) · [Exchange public trades](https://docs.cdp.coinbase.com/exchange/rest-api/market-data/get-trades) · [WebSocket feed overview](https://docs.cdp.coinbase.com/exchange/websocket-feed/overview).
86: - **Fields/data:** Candle rows contain time, low, high, open, close and volume; supported granularities are product-specific and endpoint has bounded candle count per request. Public trades include trade ID, price, size, side and time; WebSocket channels include ticker, matches/trades and level2 book messages as documented.
87: - **Access/timing/terms:** Public market endpoints do not require an authenticated key; public WebSocket subscription is available. Historical REST candles are bounded per call and may omit intervals with no ticks; paginate or use licensed historical products for deep coverage. Venue terms, rate limits, regional product availability and redistribution rights still apply.
88: - **Timestamp semantics/limits:** Trade time is venue event timestamp; preserve receipt time separately. Candle `time` denotes candle period boundary (Unix seconds, UTC in documented payload); never treat an unfinished interval as final. Coinbase Exchange is one venue and product namespace, not Coinbase-wide/consolidated crypto.
89: - **Assessment:** Grade 5 for provider docs; reviewed 2026-10-18; novelty moderate. Source type: commercial exchange API documentation.
90: 
91: ## Point-in-time ingestion patterns
92: 
93: ### Treasury API snapshot (reference series)
94: 
95: Example request: `https://api.fiscaldata.treasury.gov/services/api/fiscal_service/v2/accounting/od/avg_interest_rates?filter=record_date:gte:2025-01-01&sort=record_date&format=json`. Save request URL/parameters, raw JSON, HTTP retrieval time in UTC, response headers, and dataset/schema metadata. Treat `record_date` as the observation date, not release time. For strict PIT, archive each scheduled pull as an observed vintage and do not backfill latest corrected values into prior decision dates unless a timestamped release vintage proves availability.
96: 
97: ### ECB SDMX vintage-aware retrieval
98: 
99: Discover flow/key/DSD first; fetch the exact series with the documented REST route, e.g. `https://data-api.ecb.europa.eu/service/data/EXR/D.USD.EUR.SP00.A?startPeriod=2025-01-01&endPeriod=2025-01-31&format=csvdata`. Persist the SDMX key, response attributes/status, HTTP retrieval time and metadata version. Join by ECB observation date only after establishing the source publication/revision rule; for decision-time backtests use captured releases/vintages, not today's revised history.
100: 
101: ### Venue-event ingestion (crypto or licensed exchange feed)
102: 
103: Subscribe to a named product/channel and store every raw message with `venue_event_time`, `sequence_or_trade_id`, `local_received_at_utc`, symbol, channel, connection/session ID and payload. Detect sequence gaps/reconnects, preserve snapshots plus deltas, and rebuild books only under the venue's documented sequence rules. For candles, store interval start/end, completion status, and retrieval/receipt time; exclude unclosed bars from finalized-bar features. A polling OHLC endpoint is not evidence that the value was available at every point inside its interval.
104: 
105: ## Links and scope boundary
106: 
107: See [[Financial data source directory]] for the broader catalog and [[Data provenance and point-in-time]] for provenance cards, vintage handling, identifiers and as-of joins. Market-folder links: [[Forex]] · [[Fixed Income]] · [[Equities]] · [[ETFs]] · [[Futures]] · [[Options]] · [[Crypto]]. This note is deliberately limited to public/reference data and documented commercial source pages; no provider's coverage, best execution, or alpha claim is independently certified here.
108: 
109: ## Sources checked
110: 
111: Pages/endpoints verified in this review: Treasury Fiscal Data API response and Treasury interest-rate page; ECB API overview and FX reference-rate page; BIS bulk-download page/API docs; CFTC COT page and PRE; CME browse-data and DataMine pages; Nasdaq data catalog/screener/options chain; OCC market data/report pages; Kraken REST OHLC and API documentation; Coinbase candles/trades/WebSocket documentation. Existing parent-directory entries were checked for duplication. OCC's historical URL `https://www.theocc.com/market-data/market-data-reports/series-and-trade-information` returns 404; use the current market-data/report landing pages above and confirm specific report paths before ingestion. Product terms and schemas can change; re-check before acquisition.

- **Direct verified URLs:** [COT hub and report definitions](https://www.cftc.gov/MarketReports/CommitmentsofTraders/index.htm) · [Public Reporting Environment](https://publicreporting.cftc.gov/) · [release schedule](https://www.cftc.gov/MarketReports/CommitmentsofTraders/ReleaseSchedule/index.htm).
- **Fields/data:** Tuesday open interest and long/short/spreading positions by reportable trader category; report formats also include changes, shares of open interest, trader counts and (long reports) concentration measures. Legacy, Supplemental, Disaggregated and Traders in Financial Futures (TFF) have different universes/classification. Both futures-only and futures-plus-options combined reports exist for relevant types; TFF covers financial contracts including currencies, Treasury securities, stock indexes and VIX.
- **Access/timing/terms:** Public static reports, annual compressed files, PRE filters/downloads and API; CFTC says no API token is currently provided/usually needed, asks users not to overuse. Generally Friday 3:30pm Eastern release from prior Tuesday, subject to holidays. Data represent Tuesday, not Friday or current positions. Historical published data are not backdated/updated per CFTC FAQ. Public access; abide by site/API usage and attribution terms.
- **Limitations:** Threshold-based reporting; markets can disappear below 20 large traders; trader classes are self-reported business-purpose categories, not inferred intent. Positions aggregate and netting/spreading complicate interpretation; CFTC states suppressed trader counts below four. No price, executions, order flow, or intraday signal. Point-in-time is much better defined by release schedule, but persist actual release timestamp/calendar.
- **Assessment:** Grade 1; reviewed 2026-10-18; novelty low-moderate (parent already lists COT, this adds fields and timestamp semantics). Source type: U.S. regulator primary report.

### CME Group DataMine and real-time products — futures/options executable history (commercial)

- **Direct verified URLs:** [Browse data products](https://www.cmegroup.com/market-data/browse-data.html) · [DataMine historical source](https://www.cmegroup.com/datamine.html) · [real-time market data](https://www.cmegroup.com/market-data.html) · [data terms](https://www.cmegroup.com/trading/market-data-explanation-disclaimer.html).
- **Fields/data:** Product-specific packages may provide trade, quote, market depth/order-book, settlement, daily bulletin, and instrument/reference data for CME, CBOT, NYMEX and COMEX contracts. Exact message fields, depth, granularity, dates and symbols depend on chosen product/feed; obtain schema/sample and contract coverage before purchase. Exchange page advertises 40+ years history overall, not necessarily every product/field.
- **Access/timing/terms:** Historical downloads through DataMine are paid/product-priced; real-time streams and cloud/analytics access are subscription/entitlement products. Exchange pages distinguish real-time from delayed and historical products; no universal free executable feed. Market-data agreements, display/non-display use, redistribution and derived-data terms apply. Timestamp semantics depend on product: validate exchange event time versus publication/receive time, timezone, sequence and end-of-day convention from technical docs.
- **Limitations:** Claims are exchange product descriptions, not independent completeness tests. Contract rolls, expiries, corrections, block/EFRP inclusion, settlement methodology, session breaks and schema changes require explicit handling. A continuous series is derived, not a listed contract's actual price path.
- **Assessment:** Grade 1 for product/access facts; reviewed 2026-10-18; novelty moderate given existing directory's CME pointer. Source type: exchange commercial product documentation.

### Nasdaq public quote pages / exchange data products — listed equities, ETFs and options

- **Direct verified URLs:** [U.S. market data products](https://www.nasdaq.com/products/data) · [public stock screener](https://www.nasdaq.com/market-activity/stocks/screener) · [Nasdaq options chain page](https://www.nasdaq.com/market-activity/quotes/option-chain).
- **Fields/data:** Public pages provide security screening/listing information and displayed quote/last/volume/summary fields depending on instrument/page. Product catalog separately sells real-time and historical feeds/data sets. ETF is an instrument category using the equity market-data ecosystem; do not assume every screen field is a full ETF NAV/creation-redemption dataset. Option-chain displayed fields are not a complete consolidated OPRA event archive.
- **Access/timing/terms:** Website is accessible without an API key; displayed prices may be delayed (confirm the delay label on the selected page/instrument). Historical exchange datasets and real-time feeds require product purchase/entitlement; product and use rights vary. Page snapshot/retrieval time is not exchange event time. For systematic intraday use, license a defined feed and retain exchange timestamps/sequence.
- **Limitations:** Screen/page coverage and refresh cadence are not a stable research API contract. Nasdaq venue data do not equal consolidated U.S. market unless expressly designated. Public display quotes cannot support fill assumptions; ETF market price differs from NAV/iNAV.
- **Assessment:** Grade 1 for official page/product descriptions; reviewed 2026-10-18; novelty moderate (clear distinction between public page and licensed tape). Source type: exchange public pages and commercial data-product documentation.

### OCC — listed U.S. options reference and volume/statistical data

- **Direct verified URLs:** [OCC market data and reports](https://www.theocc.com/market-data) · [OCC data products](https://www.theocc.com/market-data/market-data-reports).
- **Fields/data:** OCC publishes options volume/open-interest reports, daily market statistics, clearing/contract reference information and product-specific data offerings. Reports can identify underlying/product, calls/puts, volume/open interest and date/contract series attributes depending on report. This is useful for option universe and activity context; it is not automatically quote/trade tick history. Verify report field definitions and download schema on the specific page.
- **Access/timing/terms:** Public report pages/downloads for published summaries; granular historical/reference products may have product-specific access/fees/agreements. Not a live executable quote endpoint. Daily report date is a business/reference date; page publication/processing time should be recorded separately. OCC data terms and any downstream exchange/OPRA entitlements govern reuse.
- **Limitations:** Aggregated volume/OI omit price, NBBO, aggressor, quote state, and venue execution details. Open interest is clearing-derived and may not equal same-day trading. Contract adjustments and symbol lifecycle must be mapped; daily snapshots cannot be used as intraday execution data.
- **Assessment:** Grade 1 for official published report/product documentation; reviewed 2026-10-18; novelty high (dedicated clearing/reference source beyond Cboe venue stats). Source type: U.S. options clearing corporation primary data publisher.

## Crypto venue public market data (venue-specific executable observations)

### Kraken public REST and WebSocket

- **Direct verified URLs:** [REST OHLC endpoint](https://docs.kraken.com/api/docs/rest-api/get-ohlc-data) · [WebSocket v2 market data](https://docs.kraken.com/api/docs/websocket-v2/ticker) · [API overview](https://docs.kraken.com/api/).
- **Fields/data:** OHLC endpoint provides pair, interval, candle start timestamp and OHLCV plus VWAP/trade count as returned by schema; last response item is current/uncommitted candle. Public ticker provides best bid/ask and related 24-hour fields; public trades/order-book WebSocket channels provide venue events/depth (channel-specific schema).
- **Access/timing/terms:** Public endpoints generally require no key for public market data; private account/trade actions require credentials. REST is snapshot/polling; WebSocket is streaming, not an exchange-wide consolidated feed. OHLC endpoint is limited to 720 recent entries regardless of interval, so not adequate for arbitrary long history. Current terms, rate limits, geographical/market availability apply.
- **Timestamp semantics/limits:** Candle timestamp is interval start (check current schema); last candle may be incomplete. WebSocket event timestamps are venue-provided and should be retained alongside local receipt time. Single venue, pair-specific asset conventions, outages, listing changes, gaps, forks and market-specific liquidity; does not represent global crypto price or executable size beyond observed book.
- **Assessment:** Grade 5 for provider-documented behavior; reviewed 2026-10-18; novelty moderate (directory already links OHLC, this adds precise cap and stream distinction). Source type: commercial exchange API documentation.

### Coinbase Exchange public market data

- **Direct verified URLs:** [product candles](https://docs.cdp.coinbase.com/exchange/rest-api/market-data/get-product-candles) · [Exchange public trades](https://docs.cdp.coinbase.com/exchange/rest-api/market-data/get-trades) · [WebSocket feed overview](https://docs.cdp.coinbase.com/exchange/websocket-feed/overview).
- **Fields/data:** Candle rows contain time, low, high, open, close and volume; supported granularities are product-specific and endpoint has bounded candle count per request. Public trades include trade ID, price, size, side and time; WebSocket channels include ticker, matches/trades and level2 book messages as documented.
- **Access/timing/terms:** Public market endpoints do not require an authenticated key; public WebSocket subscription is available. Historical REST candles are bounded per call and may omit intervals with no ticks; paginate or use licensed historical products for deep coverage. Venue terms, rate limits, regional product availability and redistribution rights still apply.
- **Timestamp semantics/limits:** Trade time is venue event timestamp; preserve receipt time separately. Candle `time` denotes candle period boundary (Unix seconds, UTC in documented payload); never treat an unfinished interval as final. Coinbase Exchange is one venue and product namespace, not Coinbase-wide/consolidated crypto.
- **Assessment:** Grade 5 for provider docs; reviewed 2026-10-18; novelty moderate. Source type: commercial exchange API documentation.

## Point-in-time ingestion patterns

### Treasury API snapshot (reference series)

Example request: `https://api.fiscaldata.treasury.gov/services/api/fiscal_service/v2/accounting/od/avg_interest_rates?filter=record_date:gte:2025-01-01&sort=record_date&format=json`. Save request URL/parameters, raw JSON, HTTP retrieval time in UTC, response headers, and dataset/schema metadata. Treat `record_date` as the observation date, not release time. For strict PIT, archive each scheduled pull as an observed vintage and do not backfill latest corrected values into prior decision dates unless a timestamped release vintage proves availability.

### ECB SDMX vintage-aware retrieval

Discover flow/key/DSD first; fetch the exact series with the documented REST route, e.g. `https://data-api.ecb.europa.eu/service/data/EXR/D.USD.EUR.SP00.A?startPeriod=2025-01-01&endPeriod=2025-01-31&format=csvdata`. Persist the SDMX key, response attributes/status, HTTP retrieval time and metadata version. Join by ECB observation date only after establishing the source publication/revision rule; for decision-time backtests use captured releases/vintages, not today's revised history.

### Venue-event ingestion (crypto or licensed exchange feed)

Subscribe to a named product/channel and store every raw message with `venue_event_time`, `sequence_or_trade_id`, `local_received_at_utc`, symbol, channel, connection/session ID and payload. Detect sequence gaps/reconnects, preserve snapshots plus deltas, and rebuild books only under the venue's documented sequence rules. For candles, store interval start/end, completion status, and retrieval/receipt time; exclude unclosed bars from finalized-bar features. A polling OHLC endpoint is not evidence that the value was available at every point inside its interval.

## Links and scope boundary

See [[Financial data source directory]] for the broader catalog and [[Data provenance and point-in-time]] for provenance cards, vintage handling, identifiers and as-of joins. Market-folder links: [[Forex]] · [[Fixed Income]] · [[Equities]] · [[ETFs]] · [[Futures]] · [[Options]] · [[Crypto]]. This note is deliberately limited to public/reference data and documented commercial source pages; no provider's coverage, best execution, or alpha claim is independently certified here.

## Sources checked

Pages/endpoints verified in this review: Treasury Fiscal Data API response and Treasury interest-rate page; ECB API overview and FX reference-rate page; BIS bulk-download page/API docs; CFTC COT page and PRE; CME browse-data and DataMine pages; Nasdaq data catalog/screener/options chain; OCC market data/report pages; Kraken REST OHLC and API documentation; Coinbase candles/trades/WebSocket documentation. Existing parent-directory entries were checked for duplication. OCC's historical URL `https://www.theocc.com/market-data/market-data-reports/series-and-trade-information` returns 404; use the current market-data/report landing pages above and confirm specific report paths before ingestion. Product terms and schemas can change; re-check before acquisition.

# Get product candles

> Historic rates for a product. Rates are returned in grouped buckets. Candle schema is of the form `[timestamp, price_low, price_high, price_open, price_close]`

<Warning>
  * Historical rate data may be incomplete. No data is published for intervals where there are no ticks.
  * Historical rates should *not* be polled frequently. For real-time info, use the trade and book endpoints in conjunction with the WebSocket feed.
</Warning>

## Time Range

If the `start` or `end` fields are not provided, both fields are ignored. If a custom time range is not declared, then one ending now is selected.

The `granularity` field must be one of the following "second" values: `{60, 300, 900, 3600, 21600, 86400}`, or your request is rejected. These values correspond to timeslices representing one minute, five minutes, fifteen minutes, one hour, six hours, and one day, respectively.

If data points are readily available, your response may contain as many as `300` candles and some of those candles may precede your declared `start` value.

## Max Candles

<Info>
  The maximum number of data points for a single request is `300` candles.
</Info>

If your selection of start/end time and granularity results in more than `300` data points, your request is rejected. To retrieve fine granularity data over a larger time range, you must make multiple requests with new start/end ranges.

## Response Items

Each bucket is an array of the following information:

* `time` bucket start time
* `low` lowest price during the bucket interval
* `high` highest price during the bucket interval
* `open` opening price (first trade) in the bucket interval
* `close` closing price (last trade) in the bucket interval
* `volume` volume of trading activity during the bucket interval


## OpenAPI

> ## Documentation Index > Fetch the complete documentation index at: https://docs.cdp.coinbase.com/llms.txt > Use this file to discover all available pages before exploring further. # Exchange WebSocket Overview The WebSocket feed is publicly available and provides real-time market data updates for orders and trades. Two endpoints are supported in both production and sandbox: * **Coinbase Market Data** is our traditional feed which is available without authentication. * **Coinbase Direct Market Data** has direct access to Coinbase Exchange servers and requires [Authentication](/exchange/websocket-feed/authentication). You can subscribe to both endpoints, but if `ws-direct` is your primary connection, we recommend using `ws-feed` as a failover. **Coinbase Market Data**
production = `wss://ws-feed.exchange.coinbase.com`
sandbox = `wss://ws-feed-public.sandbox.exchange.coinbase.com`

**Coinbase Direct Market Data**
production = `wss://ws-direct.exchange.coinbase.com`
sandbox = `wss://ws-direct.sandbox.exchange.coinbase.com` ## Protocol The WebSocket feed uses a bidirectional protocol that encodes all messages as JSON objects. All messages have a `type` attribute that can be used to handle the message appropriately. New message types can be added at any time. Clients are expected to ignore messages they do not support. ## Subscribe To begin receiving feed messages, you must send a `subscribe` message to the server indicating which channels and products to receive. This message is mandatory—you are disconnected if no `subscribe` has been received within 5 seconds. To receive feed messages, you must send a `subscribe` message or you are disconnected in 5 seconds. ```json lines wrap theme={null} // Request // Subscribe to ETH-USD and ETH-EUR with the level2, heartbeat and ticker channels, // plus receive the ticker entries for ETH-BTC and ETH-USD { "type": "subscribe", "product_ids": ["ETH-USD", "ETH-EUR"], "channels": [ "level2", "heartbeat", { "name": "ticker", "product_ids": ["ETH-BTC", "ETH-USD"] } ] } ``` You receive a `subscriptions` message as a response to an `subscribe` message. ### Unsubscribe To unsubscribe from channel/product pairs, send an `unsubscribe` message. The structure is equivalent to `subscribe` messages. You can also unsubscribe from a channel entirely by providing no product IDs. ```json lines wrap theme={null} // Request { "type": "unsubscribe", "channels": ["heartbeat"] } ``` You receive a `subscriptions` message as a response to an `unsubscribe` message. ### Specifying Product IDs There are two ways to specify the product IDs to listen for within each channel: * You can define product IDs for an individual channel. * You can define product IDs at the root of the object—this adds them to all the channels you subscribe to. ```json lines wrap theme={null} // Request { "type": "unsubscribe", "product_ids": ["ETH-USD", "ETH-EUR"], "channels": ["ticker"] } ``` ### Subscriptions Message A `subscriptions` message is sent in response to both [subscribe](#subscribe) and [unsubscribe](#unsubscribe) messages. In response to a `subscribe` message, the `subscriptions` message lists all channels you are subscribed to. Subsequent subscribe messages add to the list of subscriptions. If you subscribed to a channel without being authenticated, you will remain in the unauthenticated channel. ```json lines wrap theme={null} // Response { "type": "subscriptions", "channels": [ { "name": "level2", "product_ids": ["ETH-USD", "ETH-EUR"] }, { "name": "heartbeat", "product_ids": ["ETH-USD", "ETH-EUR"] }, { "name": "ticker", "product_ids": ["ETH-USD", "ETH-EUR", "ETH-BTC"] } ] } ``` ## Websocket Compression Extension Websocket compression, defined in RFC7692, compresses the payload of WebSocket messages which can increase total throughput and potentially reduce message delivery latency. The **permessage-deflate extension** can be enabled by adding the extension header. Currently, it is not possible to specify the compression level. From [RFC7692](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7692#section-7.1.3): The simplest "Sec-WebSocket-Extensions" header in a client (or server's) opening handshake to offer (or accept) use of the "permessage-deflate" extension looks like this: ``` GET wss://ws-feed.exchange.coinbase.com Sec-WebSocket-Extensions: permessage-deflate ``` ## Sequence Numbers Most feed messages contain a sequence number. Sequence numbers are increasing integer values for each product, with each new message being exactly one sequence number greater than the one before it. Sequence numbers that are *greater than one integer value* from the previous number indicate that a message has been dropped. Sequence numbers that are *less* than the previous number can be ignored or represent a message that has arrived out of order. In either situation you may need to perform logic to make sure your system is in the correct state. Even though a WebSocket connection is over TCP, the WebSocket servers receive market data in a manner that can result in dropped messages. Your feed consumer should be designed to handle sequence gaps and out of order messages, or should use channels that guarantee delivery of messages. To guarantee that messages are delivered and your order book is in sync, consider using the [level2 channel](/exchange/websocket-feed/channels#level2-channel). ## End-to-end Example Below is an end-to-end example for Python that handles authentication and connection to the Exchange WebSocket. This code sample can be cloned at [Coinbase Samples](https://github.com/coinbase-samples/exchange-scripts-py/tree/main/websocket). ```python [expandable] lines wrap theme={null} import asyncio, base64, hashlib, hmac, json, os, time, websockets API_KEY = str(os.environ.get('API_KEY')) PASSPHRASE = str(os.environ.get('PASSPHRASE')) SECRET_KEY = str(os.environ.get('SECRET_KEY')) URI = 'wss://ws-feed.exchange.coinbase.com' SIGNATURE_PATH = '/users/self/verify' channel = 'level2' product_ids = 'ETH-USD' async def generate_signature(): timestamp = str(time.time()) message = f'{timestamp}GET{SIGNATURE_PATH}' hmac_key = base64.b64decode(SECRET_KEY) signature = hmac.new( hmac_key, message.encode('utf-8'), digestmod=hashlib.sha256).digest() signature_b64 = base64.b64encode(signature).decode().rstrip('\n') return signature_b64, timestamp async def websocket_listener(): signature_b64, timestamp = await generate_signature() subscribe_message = json.dumps({ 'type': 'subscribe', 'channels': [{'name': channel, 'product_ids': [product_ids]}], 'signature': signature_b64, 'key': API_KEY, 'passphrase': PASSPHRASE, 'timestamp': timestamp }) while True: try: async with websockets.connect(URI, ping_interval=None) as websocket: await websocket.send(subscribe_message) while True: response = await websocket.recv() json_response = json.loads(response) print(json_response) except (websockets.exceptions.ConnectionClosedError, websockets.exceptions.ConnectionClosedOK): print('Connection closed, retrying..') await asyncio.sleep(1) if __name__ == '__main__': try: asyncio.run(websocket_listener()) except KeyboardInterrupt: print("Exiting WebSocket..") ```

# Get product candles

> Historic rates for a product. Rates are returned in grouped buckets. Candle schema is of the form `[timestamp, price_low, price_high, price_open, price_close]`

<Warning>
  * Historical rate data may be incomplete. No data is published for intervals where there are no ticks.
  * Historical rates should *not* be polled frequently. For real-time info, use the trade and book endpoints in conjunction with the WebSocket feed.
</Warning>

## Time Range

If the `start` or `end` fields are not provided, both fields are ignored. If a custom time range is not declared, then one ending now is selected.

The `granularity` field must be one of the following "second" values: `{60, 300, 900, 3600, 21600, 86400}`, or your request is rejected. These values correspond to timeslices representing one minute, five minutes, fifteen minutes, one hour, six hours, and one day, respectively.

If data points are readily available, your response may contain as many as `300` candles and some of those candles may precede your declared `start` value.

## Max Candles

<Info>
  The maximum number of data points for a single request is `300` candles.
</Info>

If your selection of start/end time and granularity results in more than `300` data points, your request is rejected. To retrieve fine granularity data over a larger time range, you must make multiple requests with new start/end ranges.

## Response Items

Each bucket is an array of the following information:

* `time` bucket start time
* `low` lowest price during the bucket interval
* `high` highest price during the bucket interval
* `open` opening price (first trade) in the bucket interval
* `close` closing price (last trade) in the bucket interval
* `volume` volume of trading activity during the bucket interval

# Get product trades

> Gets a list the latest trades for a product.

## Side

The `side` of a trade indicates the maker order side. The maker order is the order that was open on the order book.

A `buy` side indicates a down-tick because the maker was a buy order and their order was removed. A `sell` side indicates an up-tick.

## Pagination

This request is paginated. See [Pagination](/exchange/rest-api/pagination) for more information.

> ## Documentation Index > Fetch the complete documentation index at: https://docs.cdp.coinbase.com/llms.txt > Use this file to discover all available pages before exploring further. # Exchange WebSocket Overview The WebSocket feed is publicly available and provides real-time market data updates for orders and trades. Two endpoints are supported in both production and sandbox: * **Coinbase Market Data** is our traditional feed which is available without authentication. * **Coinbase Direct Market Data** has direct access to Coinbase Exchange servers and requires [Authentication](/exchange/websocket-feed/authentication). You can subscribe to both endpoints, but if `ws-direct` is your primary connection, we recommend using `ws-feed` as a failover. **Coinbase Market Data**
production = `wss://ws-feed.exchange.coinbase.com`
sandbox = `wss://ws-feed-public.sandbox.exchange.coinbase.com`

**Coinbase Direct Market Data**
production = `wss://ws-direct.exchange.coinbase.com`
sandbox = `wss://ws-direct.sandbox.exchange.coinbase.com` ## Protocol The WebSocket feed uses a bidirectional protocol that encodes all messages as JSON objects. All messages have a `type` attribute that can be used to handle the message appropriately. New message types can be added at any time. Clients are expected to ignore messages they do not support. ## Subscribe To begin receiving feed messages, you must send a `subscribe` message to the server indicating which channels and products to receive. This message is mandatory—you are disconnected if no `subscribe` has been received within 5 seconds. To receive feed messages, you must send a `subscribe` message or you are disconnected in 5 seconds. ```json lines wrap theme={null} // Request // Subscribe to ETH-USD and ETH-EUR with the level2, heartbeat and ticker channels, // plus receive the ticker entries for ETH-BTC and ETH-USD { "type": "subscribe", "product_ids": ["ETH-USD", "ETH-EUR"], "channels": [ "level2", "heartbeat", { "name": "ticker", "product_ids": ["ETH-BTC", "ETH-USD"] } ] } ``` You receive a `subscriptions` message as a response to an `subscribe` message. ### Unsubscribe To unsubscribe from channel/product pairs, send an `unsubscribe` message. The structure is equivalent to `subscribe` messages. You can also unsubscribe from a channel entirely by providing no product IDs. ```json lines wrap theme={null} // Request { "type": "unsubscribe", "channels": ["heartbeat"] } ``` You receive a `subscriptions` message as a response to an `unsubscribe` message. ### Specifying Product IDs There are two ways to specify the product IDs to listen for within each channel: * You can define product IDs for an individual channel. * You can define product IDs at the root of the object—this adds them to all the channels you subscribe to. ```json lines wrap theme={null} // Request { "type": "unsubscribe", "product_ids": ["ETH-USD", "ETH-EUR"], "channels": ["ticker"] } ``` ### Subscriptions Message A `subscriptions` message is sent in response to both [subscribe](#subscribe) and [unsubscribe](#unsubscribe) messages. In response to a `subscribe` message, the `subscriptions` message lists all channels you are subscribed to. Subsequent subscribe messages add to the list of subscriptions. If you subscribed to a channel without being authenticated, you will remain in the unauthenticated channel. ```json lines wrap theme={null} // Response { "type": "subscriptions", "channels": [ { "name": "level2", "product_ids": ["ETH-USD", "ETH-EUR"] }, { "name": "heartbeat", "product_ids": ["ETH-USD", "ETH-EUR"] }, { "name": "ticker", "product_ids": ["ETH-USD", "ETH-EUR", "ETH-BTC"] } ] } ``` ## Websocket Compression Extension Websocket compression, defined in RFC7692, compresses the payload of WebSocket messages which can increase total throughput and potentially reduce message delivery latency. The **permessage-deflate extension** can be enabled by adding the extension header. Currently, it is not possible to specify the compression level. From [RFC7692](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7692#section-7.1.3): The simplest "Sec-WebSocket-Extensions" header in a client (or server's) opening handshake to offer (or accept) use of the "permessage-deflate" extension looks like this: ``` GET wss://ws-feed.exchange.coinbase.com Sec-WebSocket-Extensions: permessage-deflate ``` ## Sequence Numbers Most feed messages contain a sequence number. Sequence numbers are increasing integer values for each product, with each new message being exactly one sequence number greater than the one before it. Sequence numbers that are *greater than one integer value* from the previous number indicate that a message has been dropped. Sequence numbers that are *less* than the previous number can be ignored or represent a message that has arrived out of order. In either situation you may need to perform logic to make sure your system is in the correct state. Even though a WebSocket connection is over TCP, the WebSocket servers receive market data in a manner that can result in dropped messages. Your feed consumer should be designed to handle sequence gaps and out of order messages, or should use channels that guarantee delivery of messages. To guarantee that messages are delivered and your order book is in sync, consider using the [level2 channel](/exchange/websocket-feed/channels#level2-channel). ## End-to-end Example Below is an end-to-end example for Python that handles authentication and connection to the Exchange WebSocket. This code sample can be cloned at [Coinbase Samples](https://github.com/coinbase-samples/exchange-scripts-py/tree/main/websocket). ```python [expandable] lines wrap theme={null} import asyncio, base64, hashlib, hmac, json, os, time, websockets API_KEY = str(os.environ.get('API_KEY')) PASSPHRASE = str(os.environ.get('PASSPHRASE')) SECRET_KEY = str(os.environ.get('SECRET_KEY')) URI = 'wss://ws-feed.exchange.coinbase.com' SIGNATURE_PATH = '/users/self/verify' channel = 'level2' product_ids = 'ETH-USD' async def generate_signature(): timestamp = str(time.time()) message = f'{timestamp}GET{SIGNATURE_PATH}' hmac_key = base64.b64decode(SECRET_KEY) signature = hmac.new( hmac_key, message.encode('utf-8'), digestmod=hashlib.sha256).digest() signature_b64 = base64.b64encode(signature).decode().rstrip('\n') return signature_b64, timestamp async def websocket_listener(): signature_b64, timestamp = await generate_signature() subscribe_message = json.dumps({ 'type': 'subscribe', 'channels': [{'name': channel, 'product_ids': [product_ids]}], 'signature': signature_b64, 'key': API_KEY, 'passphrase': PASSPHRASE, 'timestamp': timestamp }) while True: try: async with websockets.connect(URI, ping_interval=None) as websocket: await websocket.send(subscribe_message) while True: response = await websocket.recv() json_response = json.loads(response) print(json_response) except (websockets.exceptions.ConnectionClosedError, websockets.exceptions.ConnectionClosedOK): print('Connection closed, retrying..') await asyncio.sleep(1) if __name__ == '__main__': try: asyncio.run(websocket_listener()) except KeyboardInterrupt: print("Exiting WebSocket..") ```

Rate Limits
Our APIs are intended for non-commercial use. Rate limits protect the API from malicious misuse and prevent any individual user from monopolizing shared resources. They help us manage total infrastructure load and provide fair, stable access for the full API user community.
The enforced thresholds are:
LimitThresholdDaily requests50,000 requests per dayMonthly requests1,500,000 requests per month
Rate limits are measured in two ways: requests per day and requests per month. You can reach the limit through either threshold, depending on which one is exhausted first. For example, a user could exceed the daily limit by sending 52,000 requests in one day, or exceed the monthly limit by sending 1,600,000 requests in a month even if no single day reaches 50,000 requests.
Rate limits are defined and enforced at the user level across all tokens created by that user. Each user can create a maximum of five tokens. Requests made through any of those tokens count toward the same daily and monthly totals.
All API responses include rate-limit metadata in the HTTP headers so you can monitor current usage, remaining requests, and reset timing.
What happens when a limit is exceeded?
When a user exceeds a rate limit, the API returns a 429 Too Many Requests HTTP status code.
If the daily limit is reached, further requests from that user are blocked across all of the user's tokens for 24 hours from the time the limit was exceeded.
If the monthly limit is reached, further requests from that user are blocked across all of the user's tokens for 30 consecutive days from the time the limit was exceeded.
Tokens are not deleted when a rate limit is exceeded. They remain associated with the user account and can be used again after the relevant reset period has passed.

How to avoid rate limits
Exercise caution when providing programmatic access to the GFW APIs. Use the rate-limit response headers to track usage and adjust request pacing before reaching a hard cap.

Implement exponential backoff by retrying requests with increasing delays when errors occur.
Combine multiple tasks into a single API call where possible to reduce total request volume.
Track request frequency in real time and slow down before reaching the daily or monthly threshold.
Store frequently accessed data locally to avoid repeated requests for the same data.

- **Global macro and statistics:** IMF, OECD, Eurostat, UNData, Reserve Bank of India, and INEGI.
- **Physical activity and alternative data:** NASA FIRMS, Copernicus, USDA crop-progress data, Global Fishing Watch, FAA/OpenSky, port statistics, and scoped rail/grid leads.

The notes document release timing, revisions, access, and licensing; they also flag non-commercial restrictions on Global Fishing Watch and OpenSky. ## Progress against the goal

The vault has moved from an outline into a **substantial, linked research curriculum**. It now covers the original core areas—mathematics, economics/econometrics, machine learning, validation, engineering, data provenance, microstructure, and eight market workspaces—with focused subnotes, examples, exercises, source assessments, and access caveats.

Recent passes have made the content more specific: atomic notes now cover areas such as point-in-time joins, selection-aware inference, market-specific data mechanics, portfolio construction, and additional global and alternative-data sources. The index, plan, and append-only log track this work. The latest link check found no unresolved wiki-links.

### How complete is it?

- **Vault structure and navigation:** substantially complete.
- **Topic coverage:** broad and substantially deepened, but not exhaustive.
- **Data-source catalog:** significantly broadened; coverage, access, licensing, and vintages still need checking for each actual dataset and account.
- **Source quality:** sources have claim-specific grades and caveats; some sources were reviewed through abstracts or documentation rather than full text.
- **Strategy evidence:** the vault provides research methods and hypotheses, **not evidence that a particular trading edge works**.

### Remaining work

The plan keeps future tasks explicit: add licensed local copies only if provided or permitted, validate feeds against actual account entitlements before projects use them, and conduct strategy-specific empirical replications when a concrete research question and data are available.

**Bottom line:** the educational vault is a strong, organized starting library that substantially meets the documented curriculum goal. Its research coverage is broad rather than exhaustive, and the existence of a source or hypothesis does not establish a tradable edge.

1: # London Strategic Edge: Data Access and Dependencies Walkthrough
2: 
3: > **Checked:** 2026-10-18. Website and SDK capabilities/limits can change; verify the current API documentation and account usage before relying on them.
4: 
5: London Strategic Edge (LSE) presents itself as a free market-data archive and research platform. Its website advertises historical data downloads, REST access, live WebSocket access, charts, backtesting, and an ML Studio. The public Python SDK provides a practical programmatic entry point for market-history queries and live streaming.
6: 
7: ## What is needed?
8: 
9: ### Option A — Web platform
10: 
11: Use the free-dataset portal, charts, backtesting, and ML Studio via a browser. The pages are JavaScript-driven. Platform processing is browser/service-based; the accessed pages do not disclose the full underlying model runtime environment. No local Python package is necessary for this option.
12: 
13: ### Option B — Python data SDK (recommended for repeatable local research)
14: 
15: 1. **Python 3.8+** (SDK metadata lists Python `>=3.8`; a current supported version is preferable).
16: 2. A free LSE API key, available through the LSE data page/account flow.
17: 3. Install `lse-data` from PyPI.
18: 4. Base dependency: `websockets>=11.0` (for the client package/live socket support).
19: 5. Optional DataFrame workflow: install the `frames` extra, which adds `pyarrow>=14` and `pandas>=1.5` for convenient DataFrame-returning bulk history/dataset calls. Without it, bulk export returns/downloads Parquet files rather than a DataFrame.
20: 6. Network access to LSE's HTTPS API and WSS data endpoint. REST calls require the API key; the SDK accepts a key argument or `LSE_API_KEY` environment variable.
21: 
22: The SDK repository identifies itself as MIT-licensed, but that license covers the **client library only**, not the data. Its README points to the provider's terms, which prohibit redistributing/reselling LSE data or making it available to third parties. Review current terms and the specific source-data rights before retaining or using any dataset.
23: 
24: ## Setup
25: 
26: ```powershell
27: py -3 -m venv .venv
28: .\.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1
29: python -m pip install --upgrade pip
30: python -m pip install "lse-data[frames]"
31: ```
32: 
33: For Parquet-file-only bulk use, install the base package instead:
34: 
35: ```powershell
36: python -m pip install lse-data
37: ```
38: 
39: Set the key in the current PowerShell session (avoid writing it into a notebook, source file, or shared vault):
40: 
41: ```powershell
42: $env:LSE_API_KEY = "your_key_here"
43: ```
44: 
45: The SDK also accepts `LSE(api_key="...")`. Prefer environment variables or a secrets manager for local scripts; never commit the key.
46: 
47: ## Step-by-step: obtain and inspect one dataset
48: 
49: 1. **Obtain an API key** through the official [LSE data portal](https://londonstrategicedge.com/data). Confirm account status and current quota in the portal/API.
50: 2. **Find the exact instrument and source span** using `client.catalog("forex")`, `client.catalog("crypto")`, `client.catalog("stocks")`, or a relevant category. Inspect symbol, dataset, first/last observation, and coverage before forming a hypothesis.
51: 3. **Start with a small, explicit time slice** using `candles(symbol, timeframe, start, end)`; the SDK documents 14 resolutions from 1-second to monthly bars. Note that its sync REST query method caps a response at 5,000 rows per call and supports date filtering/paging.
52: 4. **For bulk history**, use `history()` or `dataset()`; the README says these run Parquet export jobs and count against an export-job budget. Space requests out and inspect `GET /vault/usage` or the account's equivalent to verify current quota.
53: 5. **Check schema and semantics locally:** inspect column names, timestamp zone/convention, row count, duplicate timestamps, gaps, OHLC validity, sample values, and start/end dates. Compare a sample to an independent source where practical.
54: 6. **Store a provenance record** alongside the experiment: retrieval time, exact symbol/dataset, date range, query parameters, package version, schema, data terms, and any transformations. Keep raw files immutable.
55: 7. **Only then build features/backtests.** Use point-in-time timestamps, realistic costs, chronological validation, and a trial ledger; see [[Research workflow]] and [[Edge validation]].
56: 
57: ### Minimal Python smoke test
58: 
59: ```python
60: from lse import LSE
61: 
62: client = LSE()  # reads LSE_API_KEY from the environment
63: items = client.catalog("forex")
64: print(items[:5])  # inspect the exact available symbols and coverage metadata
65: 
66: # Replace with a symbol actually returned by the catalog.
67: sample = client.candles("EUR/USD", "1h", start="2024-01-01", end="2024-01-03")
68: print(len(sample), sample[:2])
69: ```
70: 
71: For bulk history:
72: 
73: ```python
74: from lse import LSE
75: 
76: client = LSE()
77: history = client.history("EUR/USD", timeframe="1h", start="2024-01-01", end="2024-02-01")
78: print(type(history), getattr(history, "shape", None))

# London Strategic Edge: Data Access and Dependencies Walkthrough

> **Checked:** 2026-10-18. Website and SDK capabilities/limits can change; verify the current API documentation and account usage before relying on them.

London Strategic Edge (LSE) presents itself as a free market-data archive and research platform. Its website advertises historical data downloads, REST access, live WebSocket access, charts, backtesting, and an ML Studio. The public Python SDK provides a practical programmatic entry point for market-history queries and live streaming.

## What is needed?

### Option A — Web platform

Use the free-dataset portal, charts, backtesting, and ML Studio via a browser. The pages are JavaScript-driven. Platform processing is browser/service-based; the accessed pages do not disclose the full underlying model runtime environment. No local Python package is necessary for this option.

### Option B — Python data SDK (recommended for repeatable local research)

1. **Python 3.8+** (SDK metadata lists Python `>=3.8`; a current supported version is preferable).
2. A free LSE API key, available through the LSE data page/account flow.
3. Install `lse-data` from PyPI.
4. Base dependency: `websockets>=11.0` (for the client package/live socket support).
5. Optional DataFrame workflow: install the `frames` extra, which adds `pyarrow>=14` and `pandas>=1.5` for convenient DataFrame-returning bulk history/dataset calls. Without it, bulk export returns/downloads Parquet files rather than a DataFrame.
6. Network access to LSE's HTTPS API and WSS data endpoint. REST calls require the API key; the SDK accepts a key argument or `LSE_API_KEY` environment variable.

The SDK repository identifies itself as MIT-licensed, but that license covers the **client library only**, not the data. Its README points to the provider's terms, which prohibit redistributing/reselling LSE data or making it available to third parties. Review current terms and the specific source-data rights before retaining or using any dataset.

## Setup

```powershell
py -3 -m venv .venv
.\.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1
python -m pip install --upgrade pip
python -m pip install "lse-data[frames]"
```

For Parquet-file-only bulk use, install the base package instead:

```powershell
python -m pip install lse-data
```

Set the key in the current PowerShell session (avoid writing it into a notebook, source file, or shared vault):

```powershell
$env:LSE_API_KEY = "your_key_here"
```

The SDK also accepts `LSE(api_key="...")`. Prefer environment variables or a secrets manager for local scripts; never commit the key.

## Step-by-step: obtain and inspect one dataset

1. **Obtain an API key** through the official [LSE data portal](https://londonstrategicedge.com/data). Confirm account status and current quota in the portal/API.
2. **Find the exact instrument and source span** using `client.catalog("forex")`, `client.catalog("crypto")`, `client.catalog("stocks")`, or a relevant category. Inspect symbol, dataset, first/last observation, and coverage before forming a hypothesis.
3. **Start with a small, explicit time slice** using `candles(symbol, timeframe, start, end)`; the SDK documents 14 resolutions from 1-second to monthly bars. Note that its sync REST query method caps a response at 5,000 rows per call and supports date filtering/paging.
4. **For bulk history**, use `history()` or `dataset()`; the README says these run Parquet export jobs and count against an export-job budget. Space requests out and inspect `GET /vault/usage` or the account's equivalent to verify current quota.
5. **Check schema and semantics locally:** inspect column names, timestamp zone/convention, row count, duplicate timestamps, gaps, OHLC validity, sample values, and start/end dates. Compare a sample to an independent source where practical.
6. **Store a provenance record** alongside the experiment: retrieval time, exact symbol/dataset, date range, query parameters, package version, schema, data terms, and any transformations. Keep raw files immutable.
7. **Only then build features/backtests.** Use point-in-time timestamps, realistic costs, chronological validation, and a trial ledger; see [[Research workflow]] and [[Edge validation]].

### Minimal Python smoke test

```python
from lse import LSE

client = LSE()  # reads LSE_API_KEY from the environment
items = client.catalog("forex")
print(items[:5])  # inspect the exact available symbols and coverage metadata

# Replace with a symbol actually returned by the catalog.
sample = client.candles("EUR/USD", "1h", start="2024-01-01", end="2024-01-03")
print(len(sample), sample[:2])
```

For bulk history:

```python
from lse import LSE

client = LSE()
history = client.history("EUR/USD", timeframe="1h", start="2024-01-01", end="2024-02-01")
print(type(history), getattr(history, "shape", None))
```

Confirm the supported arguments in the installed SDK version before running examples; SDK methods and server policy may evolve.

## Useful access patterns exposed by the SDK

- `catalog(category)` / `datasets(...)`: discover instruments and coverage.
- `candles(...)`: bounded historical OHLCV queries.
- `series(...)`: macroeconomic or bond-yield series.
- Reference methods: economic calendar, insider trades, dividends, splits, COT, financial reports, company profiles, fundamentals, and bond yields.
- Options methods: chain, recent flow, and contract candles; the SDK notes some distinctions in historical coverage.
- `history(...)` / `dataset(...)`: bulk Parquet export jobs.
- `stream(...)` / `stream_async(...)`: WebSocket streaming; SDK docs describe replay availability up to 24h before continuing live.

The exact available datasets, query caps, history depth, symbol syntax, options data windows, and quotas are account/server-dependent and should be verified in a live small query.

## Research suitability and verification checks

LSE's public pages/README make large coverage and free-access claims. Treat those as vendor assertions until tested. In particular:

- **Coverage:** check data per instrument and dates. An advertised class count does not imply complete history for each name.
- **Accuracy and completeness:** compare sample observations against an official exchange, regulator, or reputable independent vendor; measure missingness, stale values, duplicates, and revisions.
- **Survivorship and point-in-time behavior:** ask whether historical universe membership, symbol changes, delisted securities, corporate actions, and revised macro values are represented as they were known then.
- **Tick/candle semantics:** determine whether timestamps identify trade, bar start, bar close, or collection time; clarify timezone and aggregation rules.
- **Volume and market fragmentation:** FX/crypto and other fragmented markets may not have a consolidated volume figure; inspect the venue/feed definition.
- **Terms:** confirm research, commercial-use, retention, internal-sharing, and derived-data permissions from current terms before use.
- **Reproducibility:** record package version, query, retrieval date, schema, and a local hash where permitted.

Use LSE as a discovery and research data source, then independently validate any result that will support a strong claim. A free dataset is especially useful for prototyping, not a substitute for lineage checks.

## Pipeline integration pattern

Treat each LSE API/export operation as an acquisition stage, not as an implicit canonical dataset. Record the exact symbol, category/dataset, timeframe, date bounds, package version, retrieval timestamp, returned schema/count, and terms with the raw response/export. Validate that pagination or export completed, that timestamp conventions and units are correct, and that a final candle is complete before transforming it. Keep provider snapshots separate from normalized tables and experiment features; see [[Research pipeline architecture]] and [[Data validation patterns]].

### Research smoke-test gates

Before a broader request, confirm: (1) catalog entry and coverage for the exact symbol; (2) installed package version and method signatures; (3) key authentication without printing or logging the secret; (4) response status, row count, schema, timezone/bar semantics, and final-bar completion; (5) one independent price comparison; and (6) current account quota and data terms. A successful API response establishes access for that query, not accuracy, completeness, point-in-time history, or permission for third-party sharing.

## Primary references

- [London Strategic Edge data portal](https://londonstrategicedge.com/data) — provider's data and access entry point. **Grade 5** for its own feature/access claims; not independent evidence of data quality.
- [API documentation](https://londonstrategicedge.com/api-documentation) — official endpoint reference; JavaScript rendering may prevent complete text extraction in some clients. **Grade 5** for product/API behavior.
- [Terms of Service](https://londonstrategicedge.com/terms) — review current terms before use. **Grade 5** for provider's contractual terms; obtain legal guidance as needed for institutional use.
- [Public `lse-data` SDK README](https://github.com/londonstrategicedge/lse-data) — setup, examples, methods, data claims, and licensing note. **Grade 5** for SDK behavior; vendor-published coverage claims should be independently tested.
- [SDK `pyproject.toml`](https://github.com/londonstrategicedge/lse-data/blob/main/pyproject.toml) — Python version and dependency metadata. **Grade 5** for package metadata.
- [[Market data]] · [[Feature engineering]] · [[Forex]] · [[Crypto]] · [[ETFs]] · [[Options]]

## Copyright and files

No article or proprietary dataset was copied into the vault. SDK/package source is linked to its public repository; follow that repository's license for code. The market data's license is separate and its terms restrict redistribution. The user can provide source files that they are licensed to share, if needed for the research environment.

Confirm terms, quotas, coverage, timestamp semantics, revisions, and entity mappings before use. Provider feature claims are generally **Grade 5** until independently validated; official primary records are strong evidence of what the agency published, but not automatically of real-time tradability.

## Official economic and macroeconomic data

| Source | Useful material | Access / timing facts | Caveats and research use |
|---|---|---|---|

Observation calls support real-time periods, vintage dates, and output types including initial-release observations. | Current FRED views may show revised histories; use ALFRED/vintage parameters for point-in-time experiments. Track reference period vs release time and exact transformation. Official API/docs: **Grade 1** for documented service semantics. |
| [BLS Public Data API](https://www.bls.gov/developers/) | CPI, employment, wages, productivity, labor-market and price series. | API v2 offers registered and unregistered access with different limits/features; supports JSON and batch requests. | Check series-specific preliminary/revised footnotes, historical benchmark revisions, release calendars, and data status. The developer page is maintained by BLS; **Grade 1** for API terms stated there. |
| [BEA API and economic accounts](https://www.bea.gov/data) | GDP, personal income/spending, national/international/regional/industry accounts. | API key registration; source website includes release schedules and methodological documentation. | National accounts are revised. Capture release vintages and definitions; do not treat reference-quarter date as availability date. **Grade 1** for official published series and definitions. |
| [World Bank Indicators API](https://datahelpdesk.worldbank.org/knowledgebase/articles/889392-about-the-indicators-api-documentation) | Cross-country economic/development indicators from multiple databases. | V2 API; documentation says no API key is required. | Mostly low-frequency and often revised/estimated; not an intraday predictor. Use as contextual macro or cross-country regime data. **Grade 1** for source metadata; indicator validity varies. |
| [BIS Data Portal](https://data.bis.org/) | Global credit, international banking, debt securities, derivatives, FX, property prices, central-bank data. | Portal supports exploration and export; docs and permitted-use terms are in portal help. | Many indicators aggregate national data and apply BIS estimates/assumptions. | [Bank of England Database](https://www.bankofengland.co.uk/boeapps/database/) | UK interest/exchange rates, banking, money/credit, financial statistics. | Searchable series database with export and XML change subscription. | Read the series notes, revisions, units, seasonality, and discontinued-series status. **Grade 1** for official UK publication. |

*** Begin Patch
*** Add File: Research/Data/Exhaustive dataset inventory and transformation protocol.md
+# Exhaustive Dataset Inventory and Transformation Protocol
+
+This protocol turns a provider catalog into a reproducible inventory and then into validated, point-in-time research tables. “Exhaustive” means every source-listed dataset/instrument/time range is accounted for as acquired, unavailable, restricted, failed, or intentionally excluded—not that every available byte should be downloaded blindly.
+
+## Current workspace status
+
+- No market-data files (CSV, Parquet, spreadsheets, etc.) are present in the workspace as of the current inventory pass.
+- The archived chat JSON is project context, not a market dataset.
+- [[London Strategic Edge]] documents catalog/history/export methods, but catalog contents, access quota, data windows, schemas, and account entitlements must be read from the user's authorized account/API.
+- The SDK license applies to client code; data licensing is separate. Its documented terms restrict redistribution/resale or making LSE data available to third parties. Do not copy credentials or restricted payloads into this Obsidian vault.
+
+## Phase 1 — Capture the provider catalog
+
+For every category/dataflow returned by the provider, record one inventory row per dataset × instrument × timeframe × available date span. Preserve the raw catalog response if the data terms allow it; otherwise save a compliant response hash, retrieval timestamp, endpoint/query, and schema summary.
+
+### Inventory schema
+
+| Field | Meaning |
+|---|---|
+| `source_id` | Stable provider/product identifier and version, if supplied. |
+| `category` | Provider grouping, preserved verbatim. |
+| `dataset_id` | Exact dataset/table/feed name. |
+| `instrument_id` | Exact provider symbol plus independent stable mapping where available. |
+| `market_type` | Spot, future, option, equity, ETF, macro series, reference data, etc. |
+| `native_resolution` | Event/tick/bar/series frequency as documented and observed. |
+| `first_available` / `last_available` | Catalog-declared bounds, not assumed complete bounds. |
+| `first_observed` / `last_observed` | Bounds actually returned in validation/acquisition. |
+| `timestamp_semantics` | Event, bar open/close, publication, settlement, or unknown; timezone and precision. |
+| `schema_version` | Field list/types, units, identifier and null conventions. |
+| `availability_class` | Point-in-time versioned, event archive, latest-history-only, adjusted/backfilled, or unknown. |
+| `license_status` | Terms URL, intended use, retention, commercial use, derived data and redistribution status. |
+| `access_status` | Accessible, requires entitlement, restricted, unavailable, not tested, or excluded. |
+| `coverage_status` | Complete against contract/catalog expectation, partial, unknown, or failed. |
+| `validation_status` | Not run, pass, warning, quarantine, or fail, with report reference. |
+| `exclusion_reason` | Explicit rationale where not acquired or transformed. |
+| `retrieved_at_utc` | Actual catalog/sample/acquisition time. |
+
+Never fill account-dependent fields from provider marketing claims. Mark unverified values as `unknown` until observed.
+
+## Phase 2 — Data acquisition in complete, auditable partitions
+
+1. Resolve terms and intended use **before** downloading. Exclude any field/product whose license does not permit the research, storage, or transformations intended.
+2. Freeze the inventory snapshot and define acquisition unit (dataset, instrument, timeframe, calendar interval) so completion can be counted.
+3. Partition bounded date ranges according to endpoint limits; persist request parameters, page/cursor, status, byte/row counts, response hash if allowed, and errors.
+4. Write each completed partition atomically. Incomplete exports stay marked partial; empty/error responses do not mean zero observations.
+5. Use bounded retries/backoff and respect server quotas. Store credentials only in local environment/secrets management, never in notes, notebooks, logs, or manifests.
+6. Resume from last committed partition after interruption and make the acquisition idempotent, avoiding duplicates.
+7. Maintain a reconciliation table: listed expected partitions versus acquired/failed/restricted/unavailable partitions. “Complete” requires every expected partition to have a disposition.
+
+## Phase 3 — Canonicalization without losing source meaning
+
+Keep layers separate:
+
+1. **Source response:** provider-native payload/file, immutable where license permits.
+2. **Parsed table:** typed fields with source IDs and raw timestamp retained.
+3. **Canonical observations:** normalized identifiers/units/timezones, preserving source-specific columns and version.
+4. **Validated observations:** QC outcomes, exception flags, no silent deletion.
+5. **Research features/labels:** separately versioned transforms with point-in-time cutoff and fitted parameters.
+
+Never overwrite original rows with cleaned or adjusted versions. Every derived row must reference its source partition, transform version, parameters, and feature-ready time.
+
+## Phase 4 — Exhaustive coverage and integrity checks
+
+- Compare returned partition ranges, counts, identifiers and timeframes against the frozen catalog.
+- Validate unique keys, pagination completion, schema changes, sequence continuity where applicable, and expected market calendars.
+- For OHLCV, check interval boundaries, OHLC consistency, units, duplicate/missing bars, and current/incomplete-bar status. Gaps may reflect no trades or a feed outage; distinguish them.
+- For quotes/trades/books, preserve venue, event time, receive time, sequence/trade ID, condition codes, and book-reset/gap state.
+- For options/futures, validate contract identifiers, expiry, multiplier, adjustment, settlement and lifecycle status.
+- For macro/reference series, preserve reference period, first publication time, vintage, correction flags, frequency and transformation.
+- Compare representative periods to an independent source only when the definitions and venue/clock match. Record discrepancies rather than silently reconciling away differences.
+- Report coverage by category, instrument, date, resolution, and validation state; include percent observed and explicit unknowns.
+
+## Phase 5 — Point-in-time transformation
+
+For each decision timestamp \(t\), use only observations whose source availability/receipt and transformation completion times are no later than \(t\). Keep `reference_time`, `published_at`, `received_at`, `processed_at`, and `valid_time` distinct. If provider history is revised or backfilled without preserved vintages, classify it latest-history-only and do not claim exact historical tradability.
+
+Use [[Data provenance and point-in-time]], [[Data vintage and real-time testing]], [[Point-in-time feature availability contract]], [[Data contracts and lineage]], and [[API quotas retries and raw snapshots]] as detailed implementation references.
+
+## Phase 6 — Coverage report and decision artifact
+
+For each inventory snapshot, generate a machine-readable report and human summary containing:
+
+- Number of listed/acquired/restricted/unavailable datasets and instruments.
+- Date/timeframe/resolution coverage and holes by source.
+- Schema/version changes and failed partitions.
+- QC pass/warn/quarantine/fail rates and example exceptions.
+- Point-in-time/vintage status and licensing status.
+- Transform versions, output counts, lineage, and cost/storage footprint.
+- Explicit exclusions and next acquisition/test decisions.
+
+Only after the coverage report is reconciled should the data be used for cross-sectional discovery or model search. Exhaustive acquisition expands researcher degrees of freedom; maintain a trial ledger and pre-specify the first tests.
+
+## LSE-specific next step
+
+If the intended dataset is London Strategic Edge, use the user's local authorized API key to call the current catalog endpoints for each category, save the response according to provider terms, and populate the inventory schema above. First test one representative instrument per product type and verify history/export quotas. Do not share the key or data in this vault. The SDK examples in [[London Strategic Edge]] are illustrative and must be checked against the installed package version and current account catalog.
+
+## Research exercise
+
+Take one source category and produce the catalog snapshot, reconciled inventory, acquisition partition ledger, QC report, and point-in-time classification. A correct result may show that the source cannot support a strict historical backtest; that is a useful research conclusion, not a failed deliverable.
+
+Related: [[Research pipeline architecture]] · [[Experiment reproducibility]] · [[Data validation patterns]] · [[Data dictionary and provenance card]] · [[Source grading]] · [[Edge validation]]
*** End Patch

+| `timestamp_semantics` | Event, bar open/close, publication, settlement, or unknown; timezone and precision. |
+| `schema_version` | Field list/types, units, identifier and null conventions. |
+| `availability_class` | Point-in-time versioned, event archive, latest-history-only, adjusted/backfilled, or unknown. |
+| `license_status` | Terms URL, intended use, retention, commercial use, derived data and redistribution status. |
+| `access_status` | Accessible, requires entitlement, restricted, unavailable, not tested, or excluded. |
+| `coverage_status` | Complete against contract/catalog expectation, partial, unknown, or failed. |
+| `validation_status` | Not run, pass, warning, quarantine, or fail, with report reference. |
+| `exclusion_reason` | Explicit rationale where not acquired or transformed. |
+| `retrieved_at_utc` | Actual catalog/sample/acquisition time. |
+

+2. Freeze the inventory snapshot and define acquisition unit (dataset, instrument, timeframe, calendar interval) so completion can be counted.
+3. Partition bounded date ranges according to endpoint limits; persist request parameters, page/cursor, status, byte/row counts, response hash if allowed, and errors.
+4. Write each completed partition atomically. Incomplete exports stay marked partial; empty/error responses do not mean zero observations.
+5. Use bounded retries/backoff and respect server quotas. Store credentials only in local environment/secrets management, never in notes, notebooks, logs, or manifests.
+6. Resume from last committed partition after interruption and make the acquisition idempotent, avoiding duplicates.
+7. Maintain a reconciliation table: listed expected partitions versus acquired/failed/restricted/unavailable partitions. “Complete” requires every expected partition to have a disposition.
+
+## Phase 3 — Canonicalization without losing source meaning
+
+Keep layers separate:
+
+1. **Source response:** provider-native payload/file, immutable where license permits.
+2. **Parsed table:** typed fields with source IDs and raw timestamp retained.
+3. **Canonical observations:** normalized identifiers/units/timezones, preserving source-specific columns and version.
+4. **Validated observations:** QC outcomes, exception flags, no silent deletion.
+5. **Research features/labels:** separately versioned transforms with point-in-time cutoff and fitted parameters.
+
+Never overwrite original rows with cleaned or adjusted versions. Every derived row must reference its source partition, transform version, parameters, and feature-ready time.
+
+## Phase 4 — Exhaustive coverage and integrity checks
+
+- Compare returned partition ranges, counts, identifiers and timeframes against the frozen catalog.
+- Validate unique keys, pagination completion, schema changes, sequence continuity where applicable, and expected market calendars.
+- For OHLCV, check interval boundaries, OHLC consistency, units, duplicate/missing bars, and current/incomplete-bar status. Gaps may reflect no trades or a feed outage; distinguish them.
+- For quotes/trades/books, preserve venue, event time, receive time, sequence/trade ID, condition codes, and book-reset/gap state.
+- For options/futures, validate contract identifiers, expiry, multiplier, adjustment, settlement and lifecycle status.
+- For macro/reference series, preserve reference period, first publication time, vintage, correction flags, frequency and transformation.
+- Compare representative periods to an independent source only when the definitions and venue/clock match. Record discrepancies rather than silently reconciling away differences.
+- Report coverage by category, instrument, date, resolution, and validation state; include percent observed and explicit unknowns.

+

+

+

+- Date/timeframe/resolution coverage and holes by source.
+- Schema/version changes and failed partitions.
+- QC pass/warn/quarantine/fail rates and example exceptions.
+- Point-in-time/vintage status and licensing status.
+- Transform versions, output counts, lineage, and cost/storage footprint.
+- Explicit exclusions and next acquisition/test decisions.

+Only after the coverage report is reconciled should the data be used for cross-sectional discovery or model search. Exhaustive acquisition expands researcher degrees of freedom; maintain a trial ledger and pre-specify the first tests.

First test one representative instrument per product type and verify history/export quotas. Do not share the key or data in this vault.
